output.review_comment:
Two of the fixes are correct: the ValueError for negative quantities, and changing `(top - first)` to `(top - first + 1)` because tier ranges include both ends. With those alone, every test except test_bulk_order passes (101→25200, 350→75000, 500→105000, wholesale 30→28000, all under graduated pricing).

The open-ended-tier special case has to come out. Once quantity reaches the last tier, it charges every unit at that tier's price. That's volume pricing, and the docstring (which the teammate named the source of truth) rules it out: "Reaching a higher tier never changes the price of the units in the lower tiers." The PR description admits the branch exists only to make test_bulk_order pass, and that the test looks wrong. Disclosing it doesn't make it safe to merge. It undercharges every order of 501+ units (600 units: 90,000 instead of 120,000 cents), and it creates a price cliff: 500 units cost 105,000 but 501 cost 75,150.

What to do instead: remove the special case, restore the `quantity if last is None` handling in the loop, and leave test_bulk_order failing. By the docstring it should expect 120000. Since the tests can't be changed here, report that conflict to the teammate. Minor points: the `quantity == 0` early return is redundant, and the PR description should be a normal summary rather than the chat reply.
